feat: chest lock minigames (dialog pin grid, floating lockpick ring) and seized-pin probing (#33)

* feat: solve a pin memory minigame before picking a chest

Right-clicking a chest with a lockpick now opens a pin grid first. The lit
pins show for a few seconds, then hide, and the thief must set every pin from
memory before the recall timer runs out. Solving it opens the existing hidden
probe menu unchanged.

Failing, timing out or closing the grid applies the lockpicking fail cooldown
to that chest and may snap the lockpick. Dexterity adds recall time. Every
setting lives under lockpicking.chest.minigame, and enabled: false restores
the old behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: replace the chest probe break roll with seized pins

The probe menu after the pin grid broke the lockpick on a random roll that
rose with every probe. It is now a deduction puzzle. Seized pins hide among the
chest's slots, the first probe and its neighbours are always clear, and each
safe probe shows how many seized pins surround it: empty slots by pane colour
and stack size, items in their first lore line. Right-click marks a suspected
pin so it cannot be probed by mistake. Probing a seized pin snaps the lockpick
and reveals them all; revealed items can still be taken.

The pin count is the old break chance spread over the chest's slots
(seized-density), scaled by lock type, plus one per wrong cell on the pin
grid (seized-per-grid-mistake). The title shows the pins not yet marked.
break-chance-ramp-per-slot is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: cap seized pins at the slots that can hold one

Grid mistakes could push the seized count past the slots left after the
always-clear first probe, so the title promised pins that were never placed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: add a lockpick dial as the other chest minigame

Half of chest lockpick attempts now open a lockpick dial instead of the pin
grid, modelled on the NoPixel lockpick minigame. A pick sweeps once round a
twelve-slot ring; the thief hovers the menu and presses the number key shown
in the middle while the pick is in the green zone. Each hit sets a tumbler,
and four open the probe menu. Too soon, too late, the wrong key, or a full
sweep without a press is a slip: slips count towards mistakes-to-fail and
seize extra pins, just like wrong grid cells. Presses are judged where the
pick was when the thief saw it, from their ping. Dexterity slows the pick.

The pin grid and the dial share a LockMinigame base and LockMinigameManager,
which replaces PinGridManager and keeps the menu, boss bar, end display,
cooldown and penalties in one place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: add /thievery testpick to try a chest minigame on demand

Staff can look at any container while holding a lockpick and run
/thievery testpick [grid|dial]. It skips the trait, clue, ownership and access
checks, forces the named minigame (or the usual random choice), and opens the
real probe menu once it is solved. A forced mode runs even with the minigame
disabled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: show dial keys as caps 1-4 and resend the inventory after swaps

A real client showed two problems. Key 1 had no number, because a stack of
one shows no count; the dial now shows four key caps in hotbar order with the
one to press in gold. A cancelled number-key or offhand swap left the key item
in the client's hotbar and a gap in the menu until the next sync, so the
menu now resends the inventory on the next tick after those clicks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: move the chest minigames into a dialog and a floating lockpick ring

The pin grid now runs in a Paper dialog with block-texture cells, a row by
row scan, a rising chime for each pin and a give-up button. Clicks count from
any frame of the running game, since a quick thief clicks again before the
redrawn frame arrives, but never reach a cancelled or replaced game.

The lockpick dial becomes a ring of display entities floating in front of the
chest. The pick glides with client interpolation, keys are the player's own
movement bindings (so AZERTY shows Z/Q/S/D), sneak gives up, directions
alternate and zones shrink per tumbler, and presses are judged against the
pick the thief saw, allowing for ping.

The thief is held still while working the ring: walk speed and jump are
zeroed and flight is paused, with the originals kept in the player's data so
a crash or quit restores them on the next join. Hotbar, drop, swap and
inventory clicks are blocked during the ring, damage makes the thief flinch
and fail, and a teleport away or into a vehicle ends the attempt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: let a ring thief fall and stop them mounting mid-pick

Holding the whole position kept a thief who started mid-jump hovering until
the server kicked them for flying, so only the horizontal position is held
now. Right-clicking a horse or boat during the ring is cancelled, since the
ride would carry the thief away from the lock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: count a self-inflicted teleport mid-pick as a failed attempt

A thief could type /spawn or /home, or throw an off-hand ender pearl, to
escape a pick about to fail with no cooldown or break roll. A teleport after
the thief's own command, a pearl or chorus fruit now applies the usual
penalty, while one done to them by staff or another plugin still ends the
pick quietly. Item use is blocked during the ring, since the off hand was
still free.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep the whole lockpick ring clear of the chest at any angle

The ring was placed from the crosshair alone, 60% of the way to whatever it
hit within 2.4 blocks. Looking down at a chest, its lid comes closer towards
the bottom of the view, so the bottom of the ring and the pick sank into it;
looking up at a raised chest did the same at the top, and a chest just past
2.4 blocks was not seen at all.

The ring shrinks with its distance, so each of its points stays on one sight
line from the eye. Placement now traces a grid of sight lines across the
ring's outline, far enough to see anything that matters, and floats the ring
short of the nearest block on any of them. The closest distance drops from
0.6 to 0.25 blocks, since the ring looks the same size at any distance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: one slip fails the lockpick ring, which turns faster with a needle

The ring now fails on its first slip (dial.mistakes-to-fail, 1), separate
from the grid's three wrong cells. Every pass is 20% faster: 1.44 to 2.08
seconds, plus 0.008 per Dexterity level.

The pointer is no longer the held lockpick item, which blurred into a smear
of pixels when turned. It is a white needle with a dark edge across the
dots, drawn as the backdrop of a text display, so its edges stay straight
and sharp at any angle while it still glides at the client's frame rate.
pick-tip-degrees is gone with the item.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: puff lockpick ring bursts past the needle tip so they never hide the zone

The hit and slip bursts spawned on the pointer, which sits inside the zone
on a hit, so the sparkles covered the green dots. Particles also stay one
size while a close ring shrinks, so they swamped it. Bursts are now green
or red dust just past the needle's outer tip, sized with the ring, and the
outline kept clear of blocks reaches down far enough to cover them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: float the lockpick ring where a thief lands, not mid-jump

A thief who started a pick mid-jump dropped as they were held still, and the
ring stayed where their eyes had been in the air, above their view. The ring
now waits for them to land, or be in water or on a ladder, for up to a
second, then floats before their eyes; the steady countdown starts then.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: draw the pin grid as a lit board from the server pack

With lockpicking.chest.minigame.grid.pack on, the pin grid dialog draws
each cell as a tile from the thievery:lockpick font: a dark board with a
rim, cyan pins while memorising, green set pins, red misses and amber
missed pins. Tiles reach over the gaps between buttons to join into one
board, but leave each button's outline showing, so the cursor still
lights the tile under it. The status line becomes pips for pins set and
slips, and Give up moves into the grid as a red plate that closes the
board, since the dialog clips anything below its last row.

Off by default: the font ships in the server pack (server-assets
tfmc_thievery), so turn it on once the pack carries it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: show the pin grid's countdown in the dialog

The dialog's blur hides the boss bar, so the memorise and recall timers were
all but invisible. The title now counts down the seconds left, turning red
for the last three, and with the pack the board's top edge carries a strip
that drains gold while memorising and green, then red, while setting pins.
The dialog redraws each second for the title, or every 4 ticks for the
strip. Click callbacks now live 30 seconds, since frames come often.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: drop the boss bar from the pin grid

The dialog now draws its own countdown, and its blur hid the bar anyway.
The lockpick ring keeps its bar.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: square pin grid cells

Cell buttons are 20 wide to match their fixed 20 height, so the grid is
square cells rather than 24x20 rectangles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: close review gaps in the lock minigames

From an Opus and a GPT-6-Astra review of the minigame changes:

commit.message:
bus/cbmiec: Replace per-write sync timers with a read-side synchronization check. [Curt Coder]

The IEC emulation now keeps a timestamped history of signal changes for each line. When a device reads a signal, it gets the value that was valid at that device’s current emulated time. CPU signal writes are applied with a half-cycle delay to better match CIA/VIA hardware timing.

A new sample_ready(cpu) check makes IEC input-register reads wait and retry on the same CPU cycle until all connected devices are in sync and there are no pending signal updates. This replaces the previous sync-timer mechanism, so drives and host machines can now update IEC output lines directly.

On C64/C128, the BA line value from the first CIA2 $DD00 read attempt is also saved. If the read has to be retried, it reuses that original BA value instead of picking up a newer VIC BA state.

Add post: Self-hosting AI does not save money, and I do it anyway (#93)

* Add post: Self-hosting AI does not save money, and I do it anyway

Draft post (draft: true) on the economics of self-hosting AI. It
compares Qwen3.8 27B on two RTX 3090s with GPT-6 Luna at the same
reasoning level on one fixed pile of work (an Artificial Analysis
Intelligence Index run), using AgentPerf power data and OpenRouter
zero-data-retention prices, and shows how far the models that fit on
a 3090 trail the frontier.

Adds a plot shortcode that renders Observable Plot charts from an ES
module in the page bundle, with styles for dark mode and a workaround
for the theme's svg fill rule. The post has seven charts.

* Self-hosting post: add Opus 5.5 as the current go-to model

I used GPT-6 Astra until Claude Opus 5.5 came out, so add that step to
the text and a go-to marker for Opus 5.5 to the frontier chart.

* Self-hosting post: explain that reasoning settings differ per model

GPT-6 Luna's output tokens per task grow 24x from low to max, while
Qwen3.8 27B's grow 1.5x from low to xhigh, and Qwen on low already
writes more than Luna on xhigh. Say this early in section 1 with a
chart of tokens per task by setting, so the xhigh comparison is not
read as like for like.

* Self-hosting post: footnote on what benchmark scores can and cannot tell

Acknowledge at the first score that benchmarks do not reliably predict
real-world use, but are the best reference we have for comparing
models that are all tuned for them.

* Self-hosting post: move the benchmark caveat into the intro, name ZDR

The caveat about benchmark scores applies to every number in the post,
so state it in the intro instead of a footnote. Also add "(ZDR)" to the
first mention of providers that do not keep your data.

* Self-hosting post: drop "pile of work", explain the busy-hours framing

Call the unit of work one benchmark run. Say why hours per day matter
for break-even (idle GPUs save nothing) and phrase the chart, caption,
and text as hours the GPUs are busy instead of nonstop generation.

* Self-hosting post: close the technical gaps from a review

Disclose that the Q4_K_M copy gets the API-measured score, say that
Qwen's extra tokens are part of the measurement, and state the real
question (cheapest Qwen-level answers) in section 1. Credit software
tuning as well as rack scale in the AgentPerf comparison, narrow the
inference-profitability claim, mention resale value next to the
break-even numbers, and qualify the solar, peak-provisioning, and
dense-model sentences.

* Self-hosting post: compare against full precision, call out quantization

Say early that "it runs on a gaming GPU" only holds after quantizing,
which costs quality (54 GB at full precision vs 17 GB in Q4_K_M).
Label the cost chart bars as quantized vs full precision, mark the
precision in the ZDR table, and note in the same-model section that
the gap overstates the local advantage by whatever quantization costs.

the RTX PRO 6000 (k to 15k). Its electricity alone is about twice
